title: Introduce Explainable Regression Inspector and adaptive stratified sampler for canaries
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Continuous canary signals are great at detecting regressions but often leave engineers blind about why a regression happened. This PR adds an "Explainable Regression Inspector" to the perf-canary pipeline: a lightweight, streaming attribution layer that produces cohort- and feature-level attributions alongside existing latency/throughput detectors, plus an adaptive stratified sampler that preserves rare but high-risk cohorts. The goal is faster RCA and safer automated rollouts.

What this change introduces: 1) Streaming attribution processor that ingests perf events and emits per-cohort attribution vectors (approximate SHAP-style contributions using a fast linear-interaction sketch). 2) Adaptive stratified sampler that decides which requests to keep for detailed tracing/kv-capture based on attribution uncertainty and recent cohort volatility. 3) New "deferred cutover" rollout guard: a canary gate that requires attribution weights for top-N contributing features to stabilize (moving window) before completing a cutover. 4) Telemetry and dashboards: new metrics (inspector.attribution_entropy, inspector.top_feature_shift, inspector.sampler_retention_pct) and a correlation heatmap UI under Observability -> Perf Canary. 5) Backward-compatible event schema v2 extension (perf_event.v2) with optional attribution blob. 6) End-to-end canary job and smoke tests added to CI.

Implementation notes: The inspector is implemented as a streaming service (inspector-worker) colocated with canary aggregators; it uses feature hashing and a lightweight online interaction estimator to bound memory usage. Sampling decisions are soft (tagged) so downstream systems can ignore them if they don't understand the tag. Attribution computation is tunable (fast-mode vs. accurate-mode) via the canary policy YAML. The deferred cutover gate plugs into the existing rollout orchestration by subscribing to canary evaluation events and rejecting completes until stabilization criteria pass.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for the estimator and sampler (coverage added). Integration tests that run against the local canary harness (perf-canary/test/harness) with synthetic traffic profiles to validate attribution correctness and sampler retention targets. An e2e canary run was executed in the staging cluster (see CI run perf-canary-e2e/824159). Memory and CPU profile runs included to ensure inspector_worker stays below the cluster resource SLOs.

Runbook / Rollout: Default rollout is disabled; operators can opt-in by setting canary.policy.inspector.enabled: true. When enabled, the default deferred-cutover window is 30 minutes with a conservative entropy threshold. The PR adds a runbook at docs/runbooks/explainable_inspector.md with troubleshooting steps for noisy attributions and guidance for tuning the sampler.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] e2e canary smoke - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Observability dashboards - [x] Backwards-compatible schema extension

Related: ENG-1289 ties to the global canary observability effort; SUP-4821 is a customer-reported case where cohort attribution would have sped RCA.

review_comments: Anika Rao: The estimator looks promising but memory usage needs a hard cap; please add a circuit breaker or an LRU eviction for the hash buckets.
Maya Chen: Added a soft-LRU and a max_buckets config with sane defaults; included stress test results in the PR description.
Jonas Keller: Can we ensure the sampler tags are optional so older services don't break? request: add backwards compatibility note.
Maya Chen: Sampler tags are optional and ignored by downstream if unknown; added explicit doc and comment in proto.
Priya Nair: Approved after e2e pass and addressing the memory cap comment.
ci_summary: e2e: perf-canary-e2e (staging) — pass after one rerun (flake in harness)
release_notes: Adds a new Explainable Regression Inspector to perf-canary: streaming attributions, adaptive stratified sampling, and a deferred-cutover rollout guard. Default off; enables richer RCA and safer automated rollouts when turned on.
notes_for_operators: Default configuration keeps inspector disabled. To enable in an existing canary policy set canary.policy.inspector.enabled=true and tune inspector.window_mins / inspector.entropy_threshold. If operator sees high attribution entropy for many cohorts, increase sampler retention_pct or reduce feature hashing resolution.
